Custom commands and the MVC comparison

Connect a WPF button to a command and compare that job with an MVC controller action.

Open interactive lesson and complete code

What you are building

A desktop student form with clear responsibilities

Build a WPF screen whose values and buttons connect to a ViewModel. The form checks input and refreshes when values change.

This example keeps its working student list in memory.

Check the result

Type a name and age, watch whether the Add button is enabled, then add a student to the list.

A command is a reusable button action with a second question: “Am I allowed to run right now?”

How to test this example in Visual Studio

Download the project below, extract it into its own folder, then open StudyLab.csproj. Wait for NuGet restore. Choose Build → Build Solution. For console projects choose Start Without Debugging. For API projects use View → Terminal, make sure the terminal is in the folder containing StudyLab.csproj, then run the command shown in the lesson. Do not paste all files into Program.cs: use the exact file names displayed below.

ICommand parts

Execute performs the action. CanExecute decides whether the action is enabled. CanExecuteChanged tells the UI to ask again. RelayCommand wraps an Action and Func<bool> so the ViewModel does not need a new class for every action. 

AddCommand = new RelayCommand(AddStudent, CanAddStudent);
// When Name or AgeText changes:
AddCommand.Refresh();

Build the MVC equivalent

For the web requirement, open project 07-mvc-client from Unit2. Run API02 on5100 and MVC07 on5200. In MVC the controller receives a new HTTP request and returns HTML/redirects. In WPF a ViewModel stays alive with the window and notifications refresh bindings. MVC forms use antiforgery protection; WPF commands do not use web antiforgery tokens. Both must validate data and keep reusable business rules out of presentation markup.

Make an improvement

Add a Clear command that empties Name and AgeText. It should be enabled when either has text. Add a SelectedStudent property and a Delete command enabled only when a list item is selected. In the web version, Delete is a POST form that then asks the API to DELETE the resource.

Try it yourself

Why call CanExecuteChanged after editing Name?

Worked answer

The button needs to recalculate whether it can run. Without notification, enabled state can become stale.

Can a WPF command return a Razor View?

Worked answer

That would mix UI models. A WPF command changes ViewModel state; an MVC action can return a Razor View.

Predict and practise

Does CanExecute decide whether a WPF command is currently allowed?

Check your prediction

Yes. WPF asks it to determine whether the command can run.

Make one change

Trace the Add button Command binding to AddCommand and CanExecute.

Worked guidance

RelayCommand wraps the action and its availability check. MVC instead uses HTTP controller actions.

Try independently

Add a Clear action that resets the form and explain when it should be enabled.
